title: POST /v1/action/propose response
description: compliance-server to runner. 202 {status: pending, ticket} while the proposal is being built; 200 {status: done, proposals} when it is. Per category: ready (every field settled, an envelope the person may commit as <category>.json), needs_person (an envelope with the pending fields left to the person, written as <category>.json.pending) or nothing_found (no cited true: no envelope, the unfilled template would decide VIOLATED). No free-text string anywhere: never repository text, never a model name. The payload of each envelope is the category's template, leaf for leaf (payload_<category>), and a layer-M citation may only name a document of the closed list (model_line_citation). Rules JSON Schema cannot state: a leaf outside pending_fields is true if and only if a citation names it; a pending leaf is never cited and carries exactly its pending value, fixed by a const in payload_<category> (the value that exempts nothing: an exempting condition at the value that does not exempt, both halves of an applicability pair true, a dependent or cross-category assertion false), so a person who renames <category>.json.pending without deciding gets the connector's gap, never a SATISFIED; pending_fields lists every pending field of the category; at most one citation per field; line_end >= line_start; the keys of proposals are exactly the categories the request asked for.

version.description: Version of the reader contract. A new version is a new contract: every party moves together.

ticket.description: Opaque handle the 202 answer gave; bound to the repository of the token that started it.

security_updates_policy.description: Never proposed (plan R4 section 1): always left to the person, with no envelope.

category.description: The ten attestable categories: one template each in crates/compliance/attestations/templates/.

line_citation.description: A line citation of a layer-D field: a true and where the detector found it, path and lines in the tree of GITHUB_SHA and the line-range hash of those lines (same rule as line_sha256 in facts.schema.json). The runner rehydrates the quote from its own file and drops the citation if the hash does not match.

scan_citation.description: The one scanner-backed true (plan R4 section 1): the vulnerability scan of the same push covered at least one package and has zero entries.

scanned_packages.description: Packages the scan covered: at least one, so zero findings means nothing found, not nothing scanned.

field_name.description: Dotted path of a leaf of the category's template.

repo_path.description: Repository-relative path with forward slashes: no leading slash, no empty, '.' or '..' segment.

sha256.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256. Validators in Python must use re.fullmatch (or \Z): with re.match or re.search, $ also accepts a trailing newline.

model_document_path.description: Closed list of exact names the model may read: text documents only, no globs, never source code, workflows, dependabot.yml, lockfiles or CHANGELOG.md (those are read by the detectors, in the runner). Lowercase security.md is not listed: GitHub recognises SECURITY.md; whether it also recognises the lowercase name is not verified.

model_line_citation.description: A line citation of a layer-M field: the model may only cite a document it was given, so path is one of the closed list of model documents.
